    Local and species contributions to beta diversity

    Source: R/beta-uniqueness.R
    beta_lcbd.Rd

    beta_lcbd() measures how unusual the composition of each site is: its local contribution to beta diversity (LCBD), with a permutation test. beta_scbd() gives the matching species contributions (SCBD), the species that vary most among sites. Both follow Legendre and De Caceres (2013): the community table is transformed, total beta diversity is the total sum of squares of the transformed table, and each site (row) and species (column) takes its share of that sum. They reproduce adespatial::beta.div().

    Usage

    beta_lcbd(
  data,
  site = site,
  species = species,
  abundance = NULL,
  transform = c("hellinger", "chord", "profiles", "presence", "none"),
  nperm = 999,
  .by = NULL
)

beta_scbd(
  data,
  site = site,
  species = species,
  abundance = NULL,
  transform = c("hellinger", "chord", "profiles", "presence", "none"),
  .by = NULL
)

    Arguments

    data

    A data frame in long format, with one row per record.

    site, species

    <tidy-select> The column holding site identifiers and the column holding species names.

    abundance

    <tidy-select> The column holding counts. If NULL (the default), a column called abundance is used when present, otherwise every row counts as one individual.

    transform

    Transformation of the abundances before the sums of squares are taken: "hellinger" (default), "chord", "profiles" (relative abundances), "presence" (presence and absence) or "none". Hellinger and chord give dissimilarities suited to community data (Legendre and De Caceres 2013).

    nperm

    Number of permutations for the test of each LCBD. Each species column is permuted independently. Use 0 to skip the test.

    .by

    <tidy-select> Optional grouping columns, kept in the output. Grouped data frames are also respected.

    Value

    beta_lcbd() returns a td_lcbd tibble with the grouping columns, the site column, lcbd, p_value and p_adjusted (Holm), plus ss_total and bd_total (total beta diversity) for the group. beta_scbd() returns a tibble with the grouping columns, species and scbd, largest first.

    References

    Legendre, P. and De Caceres, M. (2013). Beta diversity as the variance of community data: dissimilarity coefficients and partitioning. Ecology Letters, 16, 951-963. doi:10.1111/ele.12141

    Examples

    set.seed(1)
beta_lcbd(png_ants, .by = season, nperm = 99)
#> # A tibble: 10 × 7
#>    season site    lcbd p_value p_adjusted ss_total bd_total
#>    <chr>  <chr>  <dbl>   <dbl>      <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>
#>  1 dry    MW0200 0.181    0.58          1     3.49    0.873
#>  2 dry    MW0700 0.168    0.7           1     3.49    0.873
#>  3 dry    MW1200 0.184    0.59          1     3.49    0.873
#>  4 dry    MW1700 0.234    0.29          1     3.49    0.873
#>  5 dry    MW2200 0.233    0.3           1     3.49    0.873
#>  6 wet    MW0200 0.197    0.51          1     3.38    0.845
#>  7 wet    MW0700 0.175    0.57          1     3.38    0.845
#>  8 wet    MW1200 0.165    0.64          1     3.38    0.845
#>  9 wet    MW1700 0.217    0.38          1     3.38    0.845
#> 10 wet    MW2200 0.246    0.22          1     3.38    0.845

beta_scbd(png_ants, .by = season)
#> # A tibble: 104 × 3
#>    season species    scbd
#>    <chr>  <chr>     <dbl>
#>  1 dry    phei_057 0.108 
#>  2 dry    prol_004 0.0705
#>  3 dry    phei_019 0.0594
#>  4 dry    phil_001 0.0589
#>  5 dry    rhyt_001 0.0575
#>  6 dry    tetr_026 0.0539
#>  7 dry    rhyt_002 0.0417
#>  8 dry    crem_003 0.0390
#>  9 dry    ancy_001 0.0353
#> 10 dry    mono_002 0.0343
#> # ℹ 94 more rows
